meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: usually feminine: беременная, short f: беременна

examples.trans: You're not pregnant at all!

examples.text: Ты меня за идиотку принимаешь? Никакая ты не беременная!
examples.trans: Do you take me for an idiot? You're not pregnant at all!
I am pregnant with your child, Max.

meanings.note: Habitually or in general. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.
He doesn't take bribes.
I'm not taking the knife.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, that is all.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.
Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.
Come out!

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: на даче = at the dacha; на дачу = to the dacha

examples.text: Может, его ко мне на дачу?
examples.trans: Maybe to my place, to the dacha?
In summer we live at the dacha.
There, excellent! Go to the dacha.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.trans: Could we go somewhere else?
That's a different building.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.trans: Come if you want.
And if not?
Take her if you want.

жениться.gloss: to marry (of a man), to get married

meanings.en: to marry (на + prepositional, of a man); to get married
meanings.note: Biaspectual verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to marry (of a man), to get married'.

examples.trans: And Danya will marry Nina!

examples.text: А Даня на Нине женится! И будем жить дружно и фондю есть.
examples.trans: And Danya will marry Nina! And we will live together in harmony and eat fondue.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.en: into marriage (of a woman marrying a man)
meanings.note: выйти замуж = to get married; звать замуж = to propose

examples.trans: He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

examples.text: Она вышла замуж в прошлом году.
examples.trans: She got married last year.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

заходить.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.note: Заходи! = come in!. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'зайти'.

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'зайти'.

examples.trans: Come in!
Please come in.
Come in.

meanings.note: Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?

examples.trans: So you're not coming?
So that's it.
Then make sure he does.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'flounder' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не знаю насчёт камбалы, но мне очень приятно.
examples.trans: I don't know about the flounder, but I find it very pleasant.

examples.text: Так же, как камбалу. Берёшь и чистишь.
examples.trans: The same way as flounder. You take it and scale it.

meanings.note: Round shape or life preserver. Common masculine noun meaning 'circle, ring, buoy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hold onto the life ring.

examples.text: Спасательных кругов на всех людей не хватило.
examples.trans: There were not enough life buoys for all people.

meanings.note: Impersonal predicate or adverb. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Come on, it's easy.
It's easy for you to say.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Come on, it's easy. Grab the little dog in the park and run.

meanings.note: ложный вызов = false alarm; ложный гипс = fake cast

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, зачем вам этот ложный гипс на руках?
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, why do you need those fake casts on your arms?
It was a false alarm.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'contrary' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наоборот, ты очень классный повар, понял?
examples.trans: On the contrary, you are a really great cook, got it?

examples.text: Нам надо уволить одного лишнего повара.
examples.trans: We need to fire one extra cook.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'радовать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'make happy / delight'.

examples.trans: And it can make someone else very happy.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обрадовать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and make happy on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: под мою ответственность = on my responsibility

examples.trans: It's my responsibility.
On my personal responsibility.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: declines like a feminine noun in -а, but is masculine

examples.trans: Hi, Dad!
Dad is at home.
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: С первого раза = the first time. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.trans: This is my first day.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'suspects' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I am narrowing the circle of suspects.

examples.text: Ну всё, значит, первый подозреваемый есть.
examples.trans: Alright then, we have our first suspect.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: May I go?
Let's go home.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'testimony / statements' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: За дачу ложных показаний будешь привлечён к ответственности.
examples.trans: For giving false testimony you will be held liable.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть показание.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always testimony.

meanings.en: to kiss each other, share a kiss
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'целоваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kiss (each other)', paired with 'целоваться'.

examples.trans: Come on, let's kiss!
They kissed goodbye.

examples.text: Я хотел просто в его бизнес войти. Ну давай поцелуемся!
examples.trans: I just wanted to get into his business. Come on, let's kiss!

meanings.note: to entice or pull in visitors or attention

examples.trans: It is time for us to attract new guests.

examples.text: Витя, нам пора привлечь новых гостей.
examples.trans: Vitya, it is time for us to attract new guests.

meanings.note: Dissolve a marriage. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'водиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get divorced', paired with 'развестись'.

examples.trans: You and I are getting divorced.
Speak plainly, Nina: we are getting divorced!

examples.text: Потому что мы с Димой скоро разводимся.
examples.trans: Because Dima and I are getting divorced soon.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Someone who saw what happened. Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'witness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Witnesses are needed.
She is a witness.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'stellate sturgeon' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас севрюга в меню появилась?
examples.trans: Did stellate sturgeon appear on our menu?
I have never eaten stellate sturgeon.

examples.text: Новый заказ: севрюга в белом вине.
examples.trans: New order: stellate sturgeon in white wine.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am narrowing'.

examples.trans: I am narrowing the circle of suspects.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и сужать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and am narrowing on time.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('clever, smart').

examples.text: Ты же у нас такая умная!
examples.trans: You're the clever one here!
He's a very clever boy.

examples.text: Ты же у нас такая умная! Скажи, что сделать, я сделаю.
examples.trans: You're the clever one here! Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'fridge' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The milk is in the fridge.
Whose fridge is this?

examples.text: Курица? Нет. А чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.trans: A good day.
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
